prompts: Users of our harness plugins report that tool.after hooks run out of order, that sometimes a hook never runs, and that a failing hook is silently ignored. The hook bus and the plugin are in {WS}; the README there says how the bus must behave. Fix the bus. Its public API stays as it is, the tests in {WS}/test stay as they are, and package.json takes no dependencies.
answers:
[goal] Fix the hook bus so `tool.after` hooks run in order, never get skipped, and failures surface. Public API, existing tests and dependency set unchanged.

[action] Root cause was all in `src/bus.ts` `emit`: it used `list.forEach(async handler => ...)`, which fires all handlers concurrently (out of order), never awaits them (emit resolves too early), and swallows rejections (failing hooks silently ignored). Replaced it with a snapshot (`[...list]`) plus a sequential `for...of` with `await handler(payload)` (src/bus.ts:26-35). The snapshot is what keeps a self/other-unsubscribe during an emit from shifting indices and skipping later handlers; the snapshot also means subscribe/unsubscribe changes count only from the next emit, per the README. No other file's logic changed; `src/plugin.ts` depends only on the contract. Added `test/emit-contract.test.ts` covering the four README clauses the existing tests miss (existing `test/bus.test.ts` untouched; these tests fail against the old `forEach` implementation).

Assumptions I decided: "tests in ./test stay as they are" means untouched, not frozen against additions, so I added a separate regression file rather than editing theirs; `package.json` stays dependency-free (only `node --test`); the plugin needed no fix since its notice→redact→log order is correct once the bus is sequential.

[result] `npm test`: 6 pass, 0 fail, including the four new contract tests (order, emit-resolves-after-settle, same-error rejection with no later handlers, unsubscribe-mid-emit keeps the rest running). No browser tabs/windows/apps were opened, so nothing to close.

[next] None; done. If the harness wants the contract tests upstreamed under a different naming scheme, the file is self-contained and easy to move.
